body.title: fix(response): strip error response body for HEAD requests without onError
body.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Fixes #1594

### ❓ Type of change

- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (a non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] 👌 Enhancement (improving an existing functionality like performance)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (a non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] ⚠️ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

### 📚 Description

When a route matching failure occurs (404) or a handler throws `HTTPError` without an `onError` hook configured, `prepareResponse` returned `errorResponse(error, config.debug, errHeaders)` directly. Unlike successful responses and error responses processed through `onError`, this early return branch omitted checking for `HEAD` requests. Consequently, consumers of `app.request()` received a response with a JSON error payload for `HEAD` requests, violating RFC 9110 Section 9.3.2.

This PR checks `event.req.method === "HEAD"` and returns a `FastResponse` with a `null` body while preserving the status, status text, and error headers.

### 📝 Checklist

- [x] I have linked an issue or discussion.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly.
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.
- [x] I have verified that all existing and new tests pass locally.

body.title: fix(response): omit HEAD body for default errors
body.body:
Resolves #1594.

Without an `onError` hook, a missing HEAD route or a handler throwing `HTTPError` returns a JSON body through the web Response API. Node's HTTP transport strips it, and a no-op `onError` hook already makes the web response body empty.

Let the generated default error response continue through the existing Response normalization path so HEAD bodies are removed consistently. The implementation changes one line; error serialization, status/statusText, error headers, cookies, and public APIs remain unchanged.

The regression matrix covers missing HEAD routes, synchronous/asynchronous HTTPError handlers, GET JSON responses, both hook configurations, preserved error headers, and hook invocation counts. Before the fix, three web HEAD cases fail and the other 17 matrix cases pass. The minimal reproduction is in #1594.

Validation on Node.js 24.21.0 / pnpm 12.3.4:

- Error handling and bundle-budget tests: 75 passed.
- Lint, typecheck, build, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Full `pnpm test`: 3055 passed, 51 skipped, one Node body-limit test timed out after 5000ms. The unmodified main at `66cfb8a` also times out in the Node body-limit suite; a lower-worker retry did not eliminate it. The full suite is therefore not green locally.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Error responses now follow consistent response processing. Missing routes and thrown HTTP errors return the expected status and error details for `GET` requests, while `HEAD` responses remain bodyless.
  * Error headers and cookies are preserved, and success-only headers are excluded from error responses.

body.title: HEAD error responses include a JSON body when no onError hook is configured
body.body:
### Environment

- h3 main at `66cfb8a357b6285451bad498c2c40002601fae98` (package version 2.0.2)
- Node.js v24.21.0, macOS arm64
- pnpm 12.3.4
- Direct web response API (`app.request`)

### Reproduction

Starting with Node.js 24 and pnpm 12.3.4:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/h3js/h3.git h3-head-repro
cd h3-head-repro
git checkout 66cfb8a357b6285451bad498c2c40002601fae98
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

Save the following as `repro.mjs` in the repository root and run `node repro.mjs`:

```js
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { H3 } from "./src/index.ts";

const app = new H3();
const res = await app.request("/missing", { method: "HEAD" });
const body = await res.text();
console.log(JSON.stringify({ status: res.status, body }));
assert.equal(res.status, 404);
assert.equal(body, "");
```

Actual output before the assertion fails:

```json
{"status":404,"body":"{\"status\":404,\"message\":\"Cannot find any route matching [HEAD] http://localhost/missing\"}"}
```

### Describe the bug

A HEAD request to a missing route returns a JSON body through `app.request()` when the app has no `onError` hook. A handler that throws `HTTPError` synchronously or asynchronously has the same behavior. The expected response has the same error status and headers with an empty body.

Adding a no-op `onError` hook (`new H3({ onError() {} })`) makes the body empty. Node's HTTP transport also strips the body, so the problem is visible to consumers of the web Response API.

I intend to submit a small PR for this issue, with regression tests for missing routes and synchronous/asynchronous HTTPError handlers, both with and without onError.

### Additional context

In `prepareResponse`, the error branch returns `errorResponse(...)` immediately. With an onError hook, the generated Response passes through response preparation again and reaches the existing HEAD body stripping logic.

#1490 addressed HEAD body stripping while merging prepared headers into a native Response; this report concerns the early return for default error responses.
